title: structured-gist: skimmable nested outlines for agentic-AI explanations
description:
structured-gist is an agent skill that renders explanations and process recaps from agentic-AI tools as nested lecture-note outlines instead of paragraphs. Every node takes one of four fixed roles, marked by glyph and depth: concept (-), attribute (▸), enumerator (I./A./i./a.) and explanation (↪), so prose stays confined to explanation leaves. A deterministic linter checks each outline against 16 structural rules; lint_text() returns the violations and render_claim_list() emits a JSONL claim list from the same tree.

Example

The recap an agent gives at the end of a long session, rendered in block mode. The reader sees the goal, the steps, the blockers and the next step without reading a paragraph:

- Session recap
    ▸ Goal
        ↪ Ship the 0.9.1 patch from a clean development branch.
    ▸ Steps
        i. Fresh wheel install
            ↪ The claims command crashed on --help.
        ii. Parser fix
            ↪ argparse replaced the raw argv read; three tests added.
        iii. Benchmark re-pin
            ↪ CI failed on the pinned SKILL.md hash after the bump.
    ▸ Blockers
        ↪ Branch rules refused a merge commit, so the PR was squashed.
    ▸ Next
        ↪ Publish the Zenodo draft, then close the follow-up issue.

The concept is the root, each attribute names one property of it, enumerators order the steps, and prose appears only in explanation leaves.

Install

Install the skill as a Claude Code plugin:

  1. Add the marketplace: /plugin marketplace add domattioli/structured-gist
  2. Install the plugin: /plugin install structured-gist
  3. Run it: /structured-gist [block|responsive]. No argument selects block.

Install the linter and claim-list renderer from PyPI (Python standard library only):

  1. Install the package: pip install structured-gist
  2. Lint an outline: structured-gist-lint your_output.md. The command exits 1 on any violation.
  3. Emit a claim list: structured-gist-claims your_output.md. The import name is structured_gist.

This release (0.11.0)

Added

  • A drill-down mode. A reader names one node of a rendered outline and asks for more detail or its source. The reply expands that node only, keeps its ancestor chain, and quotes the source only when the quoted text matches the original source for that node.
  • 42 synthetic fixture cases and tests for the drill-down contract.

Evidence is fixture contract only. Real-agent behaviour of the drill-down is not measured in this release.

Roadmap at 0.11.0

  • Now: hedge-fidelity axis, waiting on review of the hedge lexicon (#17).
  • Next: run the pre-registered controlled benchmark that compares five rendering methods.
  • Done in 0.11.0: a drill-down mode that expands one node of a rendered outline (#16). Fixture contract only; real-agent behaviour is not measured.
